renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: classification_mix
  title: Libraries by zygosity class
  description: |-
    Each unit is one library and the ring splits them by the classifier's zygosity class: homozygous wild type, heterozygous, homozygous edited or ambiguous. It answers how many libraries carry the edit on both, one or no allele.
    How to read: a ring dominated by one class is a uniform experiment. A large ambiguous share means the wild type fraction sits between the classifier's bands, so check the outcome composition and the clonality call before trusting the library.
    Lines and annotations: the class comes from the share of wild type reads. Above 80% is homozygous wild type, 40 to 60% heterozygous, below 20% homozygous edited, and anything between is ambiguous. These are the classifier's own constants in the pipeline script.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/templates/clonality_classifier.py
  column: classification
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: classification
  caption: libraries, by zygosity class
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: clonality_mix
  title: Libraries by clonality label
  description: |-
    Each unit is one library and the ring splits them by the clonality label the indel peak structure gives them. It answers whether the edited reads come from one clone or from a mixed population.
    How to read: clonal and likely clonal libraries carry one or two dominant indels, which is what a single edited clone looks like. Polyclonal and ambiguous libraries mix many alleles, and low editing activity means too few edited reads to call a clone.
    Lines and annotations: an indel counts as a peak when it holds more than 5% of the classified reads, and a library is clonal when one peak holds more than 85%. Libraries with too few reads are labelled insufficient data. Both rules are constants of the classifier script.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/templates/clonality_classifier.py
  column: clonality
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: clonality
  caption: libraries, by clonality label

- component: card
  id: class_confidence
  title: Confidence of the zygosity call
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median confidence the classifier gives its zygosity class, from 0 to 1, and the box shows the quartiles over libraries. It answers how firmly the classes can be trusted.
    How to read: values close to 1 mean the wild type share sits on the class target. Low values point to libraries between classes or with few reads, so open the table and look at those first.
    Lines and annotations: confidence is one minus the distance of the wild type share from its class target (relaxed by half for heterozygous), with a penalty of up to 10% for libraries under 3000 reads. The formula is the classifier script's own.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/templates/clonality_classifier.py
  column: class_confidence
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: peak_share
  title: Dominant indel share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over libraries of the share of classified reads held by the largest indel peak, as a fraction from 0 to 1. It answers how dominant the main edit is.
    How to read: a value near 1 means a single edit explains the library, as in a clonal line. Low values mean the edited reads are spread over many alleles. Filter by clonality label to compare the groups.
    Lines and annotations: the threshold of 0.85 is the share above which the classifier calls a library clonal on the dominant peak alone.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/templates/clonality_classifier.py
  column: max_peak_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.85
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: median share of the dominant indel, against the clonal line

- component: interactive
  title: Zygosity class
  description: |-
    Keeps the libraries of the chosen zygosity classes and filters every tile of the tab with them.
    How to read: pick the ambiguous class to review the libraries the classifier could not place.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: classification

- component: interactive
  title: Clonality label
  description: |-
    Keeps the libraries with the chosen clonality labels and filters every tile of the tab with them.
    How to read: pick polyclonal or ambiguous to review the libraries whose edited reads do not come from one clone.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: clonality

- component: table
  title: Clonality call per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its zygosity class, confidence, clonality label, outcome shares and indel peak statistics. It answers how the classifier called each library and why.
    How to read: sort by confidence to find the weakest calls, and compare the wild type share with the class. Peak shares are fractions of the classified reads from 0 to 1. Selecting a row filters the rest of the tab to that library.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

outputs.name: Indel position around the cut site

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: deletion_profile
  title: Deletion coverage around the cut site
  description: |-
    Each curve is a library: at every offset from the cut site, the share of its classified reads whose deletion covers that position. It answers where the deletions fall and how wide the damaged stretch is.
    How to read: an efficient nuclease edit gives a hump centred on the cut site that falls off within a few tens of bases. A hump displaced from the marker points to a misplaced cut site or a second target, and a curve flat near zero means little editing. Compare libraries of one guide, which should overlap.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker at offset 0 is the cut site the pipeline reports for the amplicon (the cut site file written by the CIGAR parser). It is a landmark, not a cut-off. This catalog's recipe leaves out positions with no indel and keeps a fixed window of 100 bases either side.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: Cut site
    x_title: Offset from the cut site (bp)
    y_title: Reads with a deletion (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: offset
    y: deletion_pct

- component: advanced_viz
  id: insertion_profile
  title: Insertion starts around the cut site
  description: |-
    Each curve is a library: at every offset from the cut site, the share of its classified reads with an insertion starting there. It answers whether insertions are placed at the cut.
    How to read: insertions that peak at the cut site are the expected product of a blunt cut, usually one or a few bases. A spread-out or displaced curve is more likely sequencing or alignment noise than editing. A curve near zero means insertions are rare in this library.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker at offset 0 is the cut site the pipeline reports for the amplicon. It is a landmark, not a cut-off. This catalog's recipe leaves out positions with no insertion.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: Cut site
    x_title: Offset from the cut site (bp)
    y_title: Reads with an insertion (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: offset
    y: insertion_pct

- component: interactive
  title: Offset window
  description: |-
    Restricts the tiles to a range of offsets from the cut site.
    How to read: narrow it to the few bases around the cut to read the core of the repair, or widen it to see the amplicon ends.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: offset

- component: table
  title: Indel position table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and an offset from the cut site, with the share of classified reads whose deletion covers it and the share with an insertion starting there. It answers the exact values behind the curves.
    How to read: sort by deletion share to find the most damaged positions, and filter on a library to follow one sample.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: outcome_bars
  title: Edit outcomes per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library, split into the outcome classes of its classified reads: wild type, template-based repair, deletion-insertion, and in-frame or out-of-frame insertions and deletions. It answers what the editing produced and how the libraries compare.
    How to read: a library with a large wild type part was edited little, and one dominated by out-of-frame deletions is a good knockout candidate. Replicates of one guide should show the same mix. Switch to counts to see depth differences.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    top_n: 8
    value_title: Classified reads (%)
    x_title: Library
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    taxon: outcome
    rank: level
    abundance: pct

- component: interactive
  title: Outcome class
  description: |-
    Keeps the rows of the chosen outcome classes and filters the tiles with them.
    How to read: pick one class, such as out-of-frame deletions, to compare how much of it each library holds.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: outcome

- component: table
  title: Edit outcome table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and an outcome class, with its read count and its share of the library's classified reads. It answers the exact numbers behind the bars.
    How to read: sort by share to see the dominant class of each library, and filter on a library to compare its classes.

- component: card
  id: editing_rate
  title: Editing rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over libraries of the share of classified reads that carry any edit, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how efficiently the guide edits.
    How to read: a higher rate means more edited reads, and replicates of one guide should agree. A very low rate means the cut did not take or the guide is inactive. Compare with the frameshift share before calling a knockout.
    Note: the rate is the share of classified reads, meaning wild type, template-based and indel reads. The pipeline publishes no cut-off for it.
  column: edited_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: frameshift_rate
  title: Frameshift rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over libraries of the share of classified reads with an out-of-frame insertion or deletion, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how many reads would disrupt the coding frame.
    How to read: this is the share of all reads, so it is capped by the editing rate. A frameshift rate close to the editing rate means almost every edit is out of frame.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  column: frameshift_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: inframe_rate
  title: In-frame rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over libraries of the share of classified reads with an in-frame insertion or deletion, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how many edits keep the coding frame.
    How to read: in-frame edits can leave a working protein, so a high value next to a low frameshift rate is a weak knockout. Compare it with the frameshift rate.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  column: inframe_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: template_rate
  title: Template-based repair rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean over libraries of the share of classified reads repaired from the supplied template, and the histogram shows how the libraries spread. It answers whether homology-directed repair happened.
    How to read: without a template the rate is zero in every library, which is expected. With a template, a rate above zero is precise knock-in repair, and low values mean most cuts are repaired by end joining.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  column: template_based_pct
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: mean and highest rate, with the spread of libraries

- component: card
  id: frameshift_of_indels
  title: Frameshift share of indels
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over libraries of the out-of-frame share of the indel reads alone, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how often an edit breaks the reading frame, once editing happened.
    How to read: values close to 100% mean nearly every indel shifts the frame, which is what a knockout needs. Libraries with few indel reads are noisy, so check their depth.
    Note: a library with no indel reads has no value and is left out of the median.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  column: frameshift_of_indels_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: aligned_rate
  title: Aligned reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over libraries of the share of reads that aligned to the amplicon, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers whether the reads belong to the targeted region.
    How to read: a low share means the library holds off-target or contaminating reads and carries less signal for the editing call. Open the table to find the libraries that lag.
    Note: no cut-off is drawn, because the pipeline publishes none.
  column: aligned_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: raw_reads_per_library
  title: Raw reads per library
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median number of raw reads per library, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how deep the sequencing is.
    How to read: rates from libraries with few reads are noisy, so read them with care. A box that is very uneven means some libraries are under-sequenced relative to the rest.
    Note: no minimum depth is drawn, because the pipeline publishes none.
  column: raw_reads
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: raw_reads_total
  title: Raw reads in total
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of raw reads over all libraries in view, with the smallest and the largest library beside it. It answers how much data the run holds.
    How to read: a large gap between the smallest and the largest library means uneven loading. Open the depth scatter to see which libraries are under-sequenced.
  column: raw_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: sum, with the smallest and largest library

- component: card
  id: read_attrition
  title: Read attrition
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of raw reads, followed by the reads left after UMI clustering and the reads the CIGAR parser could classify. It answers where reads are lost on the way to an editing call.
    How to read: a large drop at clustering means redundant or low quality reads, and a drop at classification means reads that did not align or failed the filters. Open the aligned reads and filtered indels cards to see which step lost them.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  column: raw_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: attrition
  attrition_cols:
  - clustered_reads
  - classified_reads
  caption: reads, from raw to clustered to classified

- component: card
  id: filtered_indels
  title: Indel reads failing the filters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over libraries of the indel reads that failed the CIGAR parser's filters, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how much of the indel signal is discarded as noise.
    How to read: a few discarded reads is normal. A large number means many indels sit below the sequencing error rate or outside the main indel peak, so the editing rate of that library deserves a second look.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  column: indels_failing_filter
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: editing_vs_depth
  title: Editing rate against depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: its classified reads against its editing rate. It answers whether an extreme rate comes from a shallow library.
    How to read: libraries at low depth with extreme rates are the ones to distrust, and the rates of deep libraries are reliable. Points that stay apart from the cloud at high depth are real outliers. Open the table for the labelled libraries.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median edited share of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/crisprseq.
    Note: the depth axis is logarithmic.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Classified reads
    y_title: Edited reads (%)
    log_x: true
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: classified_reads
    y: edited_pct
    label: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: depth_vs_alignment
  title: Alignment against depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: its raw reads against the share that aligned to the amplicon. It answers whether poorly aligned libraries are also the shallow or the weakly edited ones.
    How to read: libraries with a low aligned share carry too little signal to call an editing rate, whatever their depth. A library that is both shallow and poorly aligned should be resequenced. Open the table for the labelled libraries.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median aligned share of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/crisprseq.
    Note: the depth axis is logarithmic.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Raw reads
    y_title: Aligned reads (%)
    log_x: true
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: raw_reads
    y: aligned_pct
    label: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: frameshift_vs_editing
  title: Frameshift share against editing rate
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: its editing rate against the out-of-frame share of its indels, sized by classified reads. It answers whether the edits that happened are the kind that knock a gene out.
    How to read: the upper right corner holds libraries that edit often and mostly out of frame, the knockout view. A point high on the vertical axis but far left has few edits, so its frameshift share rests on few reads. Large points are the better supported.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median out-of-frame share of indels of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/crisprseq.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Edited reads (%)
    y_title: Out-of-frame share of indels (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: edited_pct
    y: frameshift_of_indels_pct
    label: sample
    size: classified_reads

- component: interactive
  title: Editing rate range
  description: |-
    Keeps the libraries whose editing rate falls in the chosen range and filters every tile of the tab with them.
    How to read: raise the lower bound to study the libraries that edited well, or lower the upper bound to inspect the failures.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: edited_pct

- component: interactive
  title: Depth range
  description: |-
    Keeps the libraries whose classified reads fall in the chosen range and filters every tile of the tab with them.
    How to read: raise the lower bound to drop shallow libraries, whose rates are the least reliable.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: classified_reads

- component: table
  title: Editing outcome table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its read accounting, its editing, frameshift, in-frame and template-based rates, and the indel filter counts. It answers how each library fared, in numbers.
    How to read: sort by editing rate or by depth and compare the rates with the accounting columns. Rates are shares of the classified reads. Selecting a row filters the rest of the tab to that library.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: size_profile
  title: Indel size distribution
  description: |-
    Each curve is a library: the share of its classified reads carrying an indel of each signed size, with deletions negative and insertions positive. It answers which repair outcomes a guide produces.
    How to read: a few dominant sizes, such as a one base insertion or short deletions, are a reproducible repair signature, and replicates of one guide should overlap. A flat curve spread over many sizes means unspecific damage. Sizes that are multiples of three keep the reading frame, so check the frameshift share before calling a knockout.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker at 0 only separates deletions from insertions and is not a cut-off. Sizes beyond 100 bases are not drawn.
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: No length change
    x_title: Indel size (bp, deletions negative)
    y_title: Classified reads (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: size
    y: pct_reads

- component: interactive
  title: Indel size window
  description: |-
    Restricts the tiles to a range of signed indel sizes.
    How to read: narrow it around zero to read the small indels that dominate most edits.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: size

- component: table
  title: Indel size table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and an indel size, with its read count and its share of the classified reads and of the indel reads. It answers the exact values behind the curves.
    How to read: sort by share to list the dominant sizes of a library, and compare the two shares to see how much of the library is edited.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: allele_map
  title: Indel alleles by position and size
  description: |-
    Each point is an indel allele of a library: where it starts relative to the cut site against its signed size, coloured by type and sized by its share of the classified reads. It answers which alleles dominate and where they sit.
    How to read: the biggest points are the library's main repair products. Deletions that start upstream of the cut and reach across it, and a single base insertion at the cut, are the usual signatures of a nuclease edit. Small points far from the cut are mostly noise, so look at the labelled ones first.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line at offset 0 is the cut site the pipeline reports for the amplicon. It is a landmark, not a cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Offset from the cut site (bp)
    y_title: Indel size (bp, deletions negative)
    reference_line: vertical
    reference_value: 0
    reference_label: Cut site
    top_n_labels: 8
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: offset
    y: size
    label: allele
    color: indel_type
    size: pct_reads

- component: card
  id: allele_count
  title: Indel alleles
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the alleles of every library in view, and the ring splits them by type: deletion, insertion or deletion-insertion. It answers how many distinct edits were seen and which kind prevails.
    How to read: many alleles with few reads each is typical of noise, so weigh them by the share column of the table. The extra figure counts the distinct alleles across libraries.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  column: allele
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: indel_type
  caption: alleles, by type

- component: interactive
  title: Indel type
  description: |-
    Keeps the alleles of the chosen types and filters the tiles with them.
    How to read: pick deletions to study the dominant repair product of a nuclease cut.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: indel_type

- component: interactive
  title: Reading frame
  description: |-
    Keeps the alleles with the chosen frame effect, in-frame or frameshift, and filters the tiles with them.
    How to read: pick frameshift to list the alleles that disrupt the coding sequence.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: frame

- component: interactive
  title: Main indel peak
  description: |-
    Keeps the alleles inside or outside the library's main indel peak and filters the tiles with them.
    How to read: alleles outside the main peak are more likely noise or minor variants than the edit itself.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: peak

- component: table
  title: Indel allele table
  description: |-
    Each row is a distinct indel allele of a library, with its type, position, size, reading frame, read count and its shares of the classified and of the indel reads. It answers the exact numbers behind the scatter.
    How to read: sort by share to list the main alleles of a library. Selecting a row filters the rest of the tab to that allele.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: allele

outputs.name: Substitution and gap rate per position

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: substitution_profile
  title: Substituted bases around the cut site
  description: |-
    Each curve is a library: at every offset from the cut site, the share of aligned reads carrying a base other than the most common one at that position. It answers where bases change around the cut.
    How to read: a flat line near zero is a nuclease run with no substitution signal. A hump near the cut can mean base editing, and isolated spikes are usually single nucleotide variants of the sample or sequencing errors. Compare with the deletion profile to tell editing from noise.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker at offset 0 is the cut site the pipeline reports for the amplicon (the cut site file written by the CIGAR parser). This catalog's recipe takes the most common base of the library at each position as the reference, not the genome base, so a homozygous variant shows no substitution.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: Cut site
    x_title: Offset from the cut site (bp)
    y_title: Reads with a substituted base (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: offset
    y: substitution_pct

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gap_profile
  title: Gaps around the cut site
  description: |-
    Each curve is a library: at every offset from the cut site, the share of aligned reads with a gap, meaning a deleted base. It answers where deletions pile up around the cut.
    How to read: a nuclease edit shows a gap peak at the cut that decays on both sides. A gap level that is high everywhere points to an alignment or amplicon issue rather than editing. Compare with the deletion profile of the same library.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker at offset 0 is the cut site the pipeline reports for the amplicon. It is a landmark, not a cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/crisprseq/2.3.0/docs/output/targeted.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: Cut site
    x_title: Offset from the cut site (bp)
    y_title: Reads with a gap (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: offset
    y: gap_pct

- component: interactive
  title: Offset window
  description: |-
    Restricts the tiles to a range of offsets from the cut site.
    How to read: narrow it to the protospacer to read the bases the guide targets.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: offset

- component: table
  title: Substitution rate table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and an amplicon position, with its offset from the cut site, its most common base and the shares of reads with another base or a gap. It answers the exact values behind the curves.
    How to read: sort by substitution share to list the positions that change most, and filter on a library to read one sample.
